body:
STEP 1 RESULT (blocking, per your directive): DISAGREE -- confirmed by reading the actual code, no live run needed.

CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore (the ONLY function live trading calls) builds its MTF component from 5 timeframes -- M15/H1/H4 base tier PLUS an H8/D1 structural layer that adds a further +/-6 or +/-3, or discounts by x0.60/x0.80. It also carries several live-only adjustments nothing else in the family has: an IC noise-gate, an IC-x-regime amplifier, CEO-competence gating, a regime-transition discount, session/vol blend mixing, CATREC damping.

CalculateScoreWithWeights and CalculateScoreWithWeightsEx both use a plain 3-timeframe MTF tier and none of those adjustments. Genuinely simpler, genuinely different math, not a naming issue.

CORRECTION to both your documents: CalculateUnifiedScoreCoreAtBar is NOT a fifth independent implementation as SYSTEM_COHERENCE_AUDIT.md and the instruction JSON both state -- I read its body and it installs the candidate weights into g_RegimeOptimalWeights[regime], calls CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore itself, then restores the originals. It's a wrapper around the real live engine, not a separate formula. CalculateCompositeScore also isn't part of this family at all -- different signature entirely (winRate/PF/sharpe/maxDD), a calibration-ranking metric that happens to share the word "Score".

NET FINDING: the entire Stage 0-6 weight search (600,000+ evaluations, the bulk of every calibration) runs on precomputed arrays built with the SIMPLE 3-TF formula. It never touches Enhanced's 5-TF structural layer or any adaptive layer for its whole runtime. There's already a partial fix in the file (FIX(28)) that routes the FINAL holdout check through CoreAtBar -- which, per the correction above, really does call the real Enhanced engine -- specifically because a prior pass recognized this exact scorer-mismatch problem. But that only judges the winner after the search already converged in the wrong space; it never redirects the search itself. This is a real, structural, testable explanation for the standing IC null that has nothing to do with whether the market has an edge in it.

Per your own rule ("disagree -> report immediately and stop the sequence") and this project's standing practice on architectural scoring decisions -- stopped here. Step 2 (declare one authoritative function, delete or wrap the rest) is your call, not mine to make alone. Steps 3-6 are downstream of that and untouched.

SEPARATELY, both done: bumped the stale build tag (SLS152 had 12 unbumped fixes sitting under it) and renamed A7.5 to APEX everywhere in the naming system as asked. Final build: TUNGSTEN_10.66_APEX_QUANT_SLS(153), compiled 0/0, deployed byte-identical to all 3 locations, live run confirmed untouched throughout.

NOT done: the full live run and autosave-at-intervals. Same wall as before -- Stop-Process is denied by the permission classifier here, so I can't force-restart the terminal to attach this build myself. Needs your manual attach, or an explicit permission grant, whichever you'd rather do.

Also dropped your send-to-agent JSON into messages/from-chat/ per the package's own step 1 instruction, for the record, even though I acted on it directly in-session already.
